transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I don’t really feel happiness or closeness anymore. My wife tries to get me into our old Sunday routines, and even when something goes well at work, I just... don’t feel much of anything.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Since the retrofit accident—about a year and seven months now.
Did you sustain a head injury during the accident?

I don’t know if I hit my head. I remember the meeting before everything failed, and then the ambulance afterward, but those few minutes in between—when I was trying to give directions and help—are just broken up. Parts of it are gone.
Do you ever experience unwanted memories, vivid flashbacks, or nightmares about the accident?
Yes. A normal plant alarm, a retrofit checklist, even the smell of hot metal—any of that can put me right back there. I see him on the floor and hear everybody yelling for help.
Do you make an effort to avoid things that remind you of the accident?
Yes. I avoid that production line whenever I can—I’ll send someone else to walk it. And if people start talking about the rollout or the investigation, I usually shut the conversation down.
Have you found yourself feeling constantly on guard or watching out for danger since the accident?
Yes. On the floor, I’m always checking the gauges, the exits, people’s hands, where the emergency stops are. Even in meetings, I make sure I sit where I can see the door.
